subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Seven Across Cultures
description: Learn Seven Across Cultures in one minute.

hook.text: Seven days in a week. Seven deadly sins. Seven wonders. Seven notes in a musical scale. Seven is everywhere.

buildup.text: The Babylonians tracked seven moving objects in the sky: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn.

discovery.text: Each weekday was named after one of these seven celestial bodies. Tuesday is Mars-day. Saturday is Saturn-day.

twist.text: Seven may feel magical because of its astronomical origin. The sky had seven wanderers—so seven became sacred.

climax.text: Seven is the highest number most people can hold in short-term memory. Cognition and cosmos aligned.

punchline.text: Seven planets. Seven days. One coincidence.

quiz.question: Why did the Babylonians consider seven sacred?
options: Seven celestial bodies moved across the sky
